history.summary: Modern sun temple at Sidhgora, Jamshedpur, built by the Jharkhand Tourism Development Corporation (JTDC). The temple has three shikharas in Kalinga architecture, sits on a hilltop with panoramic views, and has two man-made ponds and a small man-made waterfall with a Shiva idol in its premises; a new Ram Mandir is under construction beside it and a park adjoins the complex (park entry fee ~Rs 5 per reviews). It is Jamshedpur's main Chhath venue: the Surya Mandir Samiti organises the Kartik and Chaiti Chhath with cleaned ponds, first-come-first-served arghya, cultural evenings and famous visiting singers (e.g. Suresh Wadkar, Sunidhi Chauhan per reports). It is also a popular winter picnic spot. This is a different temple from the Surya Mandir at Bundu (near Ranchi) and seq 1355 (Surya Mandir, Surajpur Baragaon, Nalanda). CSV town 'Jamshedpur' is coarse - corrected to Sidhgora, Jamshedpur.

name: Surya Mandir, Jamshedpur
town_description: Jamshedpur, known as the Steel City of India, is the largest city in Jharkhand. Founded by Jamsetji Tata as a planned industrial town around Tata Steel (TISCO), the settlement was called Sakchi until it was renamed Jamshedpur in 1919. The city sits at the confluence of the Kharkai and Subarnarekha rivers in East Singhbhum district, and its neighbourhoods (Telco, Golmuri, Sakchi, Kadma, Parsudih, Sidhgora) grew around Tata Steel and its subsidiary companies.

travel.airport: Sonari Airport, Jamshedpur, ~8 km (per Velpu; verify)
travel.road: On Sidgoda Road near Baridih Old Bus Stand (~1 km); reachable by auto and city bus

visitor_information.best_time: October to November (Chhath Puja); winter months September to February
visitor_information.opening_hours: 07:00 AM - 08:00 PM all days (per Velpu; verify). Photography reported not allowed inside (per YatraDham)
